newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shop hours to be extended in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shop hours to be extended in 1997.

text.p: Austrians, subject to some of the most restrictive retail laws in Europe, will win six more shopping hours a week from January 1, according to a draft law passed by a parliamentary committee on Wednesday.
Parliament is expected to rubber stamp the law in mid-December, allowing most stores to stay open for 66 hours a week and keep cash registers ringing until 5 p.m. on Saturdays.

Shutters across Austria currently come down at 1 p.m. on Saturdays, apart from one "long Saturday" each month, leaving frustrated consumers to window shop or flee across the border into neighbouring Italy and eastern Europe.
"This is a big step forward," Vice Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel told journalists. "It should help stem the flow of shoppers abroad and it also shows a readiness to deregulate."
Unions too expressed satisfaction at the draft law, which will give shop employees time off in lieu of Saturdays worked.
Church groups were less enthusiastic in their response, however. One regional Roman Catholic group called on shoppers to ignore new retail legislation.
"Buy with responsibility...,buy before 6 p.m. and if possible not on a Saturday afternoon," the group, based in St. Polten outside Vienna, said in a statement.
Austria came under pressure to liberalise its trading laws after its northern neighbour Germany freed up its shopping hours last month.

Austria's powerful unions and some shopowners blocked early attempts by Economy Minister Johannes Farnleitner to change the status quo, fearful that small stores would be squeezed out of business by supermarkets while employees would be forced to work longer hours.

Under the draft, Austrians will lose their one late night of shopping each week. In future shops will open Monday to Friday from 6 a.m. to 7.30 p.m. At present they can stay open to 9 p.m. once a week.
